Headline: Bitget plans Thai crypto exchange acquisition weeks after $388M hack
Sources: Cointelegraph, Crypto News, TradingView

Article text:
0.22%TRX$0.3322 0.34%LINK$11.92 1.19%ZEC$1,141.23 0.18%ADA$0.2161 1.14%XRP$1.29 0.81%ETH$2,386.23 1.62%BTC$81,530.19 1.05%XMR$611.21 3.93%BNB$729.10 0.54%XLM$0.1757 0.60%SOL$104.23 0.69%HYPE$78.38 1.19%Written by Felix Ngstaff editorEdited by Yohan Yunstaff editorWritten by Felix Ngstaff editorEdited by Yohan Yunstaff editorBitget plans Thai crypto exchange acquisition weeks after $388M hack Latest NewsPublishedOct 20, 2026The proposed acquisition would give Bitget a route into Thailand’s crypto market through a locally licensed operator. Crypto exchange Bitget has announced plans to acquire Thailand’s GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics, seeking to expand its Southeast Asia footprint weeks after a major hack impacting its hot and warm wallets. The proposed transaction involves BTGT Management (Thailand), a company in which Bitget says it holds an interest, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph.  The acquisition will allow Bitget to introduce its trading platform to Thai users. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations in a thriving country,” said Bitget CEO Gracy Chen. GMO Internet disclosed the proposed sale to BTGT Management in a Sept. 24 filing, targeting completion for Oct. 31. Bitget’s announcement identifies its involvement in the transaction. The company declined to comment on how much interest in BTGT Management the company holds and the financial and ownership terms of the proposed acquisition. GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics operates Z.com EX, which launched in February 2021. Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission lists the company among its licensed digital asset exchange operators. Related: Thailand crypto ETFs may see slow start despite new rules: CoinShares Completion remains subject to regulatory approval and other conditions. The proposed deal follows a Sept. 24 attack on Bitget’s hot and warm wallet infrastructure. In its account of the breach, Bitget said approximately $388 million was affected after attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party security product and issued fraudulent withdrawal commands. Bitget said customer account balances were unaffected and that it completed the phased restoration of withdrawals on Oct. 2. On Oct. 17, Bitget also announced plans to discontinue services for certain users, describing the move as a “one-off exercise.” Bitget’s terms of use, updated Oct. 16, list Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan among its prohibited jurisdictions. Thailand is also listed as a prohibited jurisdiction, although the proposed acquisition could provide Bitget with a route to serving the market through a locally licensed operator. Magazine: Scammer loses $4.8M stored on tampered Ledgers: Asia Express

305964e4cf.facts: Headline: BlackRock files for bitcoin ETF offering downside protection and upside exposure to IBIT Sources: Pluang, The Block Article text: Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here. BlackRock files for bitcoin ETF offering downside protection and upside exposure to IBITBlackRock filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protect ETF on Monday. ShareThe BlockQuick Take “The Fund seeks to provide upside exposure to the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) and/or similar bitcoin exposure up to an approximate limit, while seeking to provide a level of downside protection,” BlackRock said in the filing on Monday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust holds more than $65 billion in assets under management, making it the largest of its kind. BlackRock, the world's largest investment manager, has filed for another bitcoin fund, this time one that would give investors both downside protection and upside exposure to its flagship bitcoin exchange-traded fund. On Monday, the firm filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protect ETF. That fund will follow BlackRock's multi-billion-dollar iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, the firm said. "The Fund seeks to provide upside exposure to the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) and/or similar bitcoin exposure up to an approximate limit, while seeking to provide a level of downside protection," BlackRock said in the filing. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust holds more than $65 billion in assets under management, making it the largest of its kind, according to The Block's bitcoin ETF tracker. BlackRock launched IBIT in January 2024. In June, the firm launched its iShares Bitcoin Premium Income ETF, which is designed to provide investors with exposure to bitcoin while generating monthly option premium income. In a post on X, Bloomberg Intelligence's James Seyffart noted that BlackRock still just has bitcoin and Ethereum products. Over the past couple of years, other companies have launched ETFs tracking assets from XRP to SOL to DOGE. "Notably, this is the third Bitcoin ETF filing from them," Seyffart said on Monday. "Still only have Bitcoin and Ethereum products -- no other cryptos."

38b67748f6.facts:
Headline: Walmart Never Partnered With Litecoin. The Chart Didn't Know
Sources: Chain Secrets
Verified story facts:
Sept 13, 2021: a fake press release on GlobeNewswire claimed Walmart would accept Litecoin from October 1, complete with made-up quotes from Walmart's CEO. Litecoin's official account shared it, and LTC ripped from ~$175 to ~$233 in minutes (Binance wick: $240). Then Walmart said it has no relationship with Litecoin, and the pump was gone. Litecoin's creator Charlie Lee: "this time we really messed up." Two months later, the same trick hit Kroger with Bitcoin Cash. Real LTC/USDT daily chart (Binance), Aug–Oct 2021. Posts shown are recreations.

item.title: Walmart Never Partnered With Litecoin. The Chart Didn't Know

p.keyfact: A fake GlobeNewswire press release triggered a massive Litecoin pump before being debunked.
p.post: Never trust a headline until the chart confirms it. A fake press release claimed Walmart partnered with Litecoin, sending LTC ripping from $175 to $233 in minutes. The official LTC account even shared it. Then Walmart spoke up, and the pump vanished just as fast. #Litecoin
p.quote: this time we really messed up. = Charlie Lee
p.reply: Ah, the classic fake press release pump and dump. Reminds us that the chart doesn't care who retweets the headline.
p.thread:
1/ Markets trade on news, but sometimes the news is pure fiction. On Sept 13, 2021, a fake press release dropped on GlobeNewswire claiming Walmart would accept Litecoin starting October 1.
2/ The fake release even featured made-up quotes from Walmart's CEO. Litecoin's official Twitter account shared the news, sparking instant FOMO.
3/ LTC ripped from around $175 to roughly $233 in minutes, printing a Binance wick all the way up to $240. 
4/ The party ended when Walmart confirmed zero relationship with Litecoin. Litecoin's creator Charlie Lee admitted: "this time we really messed up." Two months later, copycats tried the exact same trick on Kroger with Bitcoin Cash.
p.timeline: Sept 13, 2021 = Fake press release claims Walmart accepts LTC ; Sept 13, 2021 = LTC official account shares fake news ; Sept 13, 2021 = LTC rips from $175 to $233 ; Sept 13, 2021 = Walmart denies partnership and pump vanishes
p.title: Litecoin's Walmart Fake-Out
